To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the K(d) values of (75)Se are in the range 0.05-0.5 L kg(-1); (2) soil moisture content and redox potential are important factors that control the partitioning of (75) Se in soil; and (3) microbial activity does not seem to be a major factor that controls (75)Se solid-liquid partition in the soil.
(1) the K(d) values of radio-selenide in soil are controlled by geochemical rather than microbial processes; and (2) the K(d)s are influenced by redox conditions and soil organic matter content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the partitioning of radio-selenium between soil and water.
understanding the fundamental processes that control the partitioning of radio-selenium between soil and solution.
the fate of radioactive Se and how this is affected by soil type, soil moisture content and redox potential.

the K(d) value of Se is a function of soil type (organic matter, texture and mineralogy), soil water content, Eh and microbial activity.

soil moisture content and redox potential can have a major effect on the partitioning of radio-selenium between soil and liquid.
